newsitem.title: UK: UK government plans rules to end late bill payment.
newsitem.headline: UK government plans rules to end late bill payment.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government will unveil tough proposals on Tuesday to stop the late payment of bills, The Times newspaper said.
The move was described as a two billion pound ($3 billion) lifeline to small firms, which often find themselves at the mercy of late-paying customers.

A parliamentary bill to give firms the right to charge interest on accounts that are unpaid beyond a specific date will be a surprise late addition to Wednesday's Queen's speech in which the government is to outline its legislative programme.
Under the legislation large companies, regarded as the main offenders, would be required to show in their annual accounts the proportion of their bills they had paid late, The Times said.
The measure was being brought forward because the government accepts that late payment sometimes forces small firms out of business.
The government will consult business leaders before fixing a timescale -- perhaps a month or six weeks -- after which it will be possible to charge interest on unpaid bills.
Government departments and local authorities were also being told to pay their bills on time, The Times said. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7717
